St Michael's Clergy House, Mark Street, Shoreditch, London EC2A 4ER

# House of Hackney showroom, St Michael's Clergy House

Preparation and making good of the 1856 clergy house, then decorating and hanging House of Hackney's own papers through the concept rooms, bedroom and tiled cloakrooms, ready for the public opening on 26 March 2022.

![Finished room at the House of Hackney showroom, St Michael's Clergy House, with dark floral wallpaper, matching curtains and low floral sofas.](https://www.mrwallcover.com/media/img/hoh-official-01.jpg)

Photograph: House of Hackney

## Project record

Client, materials & project facts

**Client**
: House of Hackney

**Designer**
: –Not recorded

**Main contractor**
: –Not recorded

**Maker and paper**

**Area or rooms**

**Scope**

**Year**

## At a glance

- **Client:** House of Hackney
- **Address:** St Michael’s Clergy House, Mark Street, Shoreditch EC2A 4ER
- **Survey:** October 2021
- **Works:** January to March 2022, before the public opening on 26 March 2022. Cloakrooms in May 2022
- **Scope:** preparation and making good, decorating, and hanging House of Hackney’s own wallpapers in the concept rooms, the bedroom set and the tiled cloakrooms

## The work

St Michael’s Clergy House dates from 1856. The brief was the interior of the new flagship: make the rooms good, decorate them, and hang the brand’s own wallpapers so the concept rooms, the bedroom and the cloakrooms could open to the public.

The survey was in October 2021. Making good and decorating ran from January 2022, and the rooms were dressed before the opening on 26 March 2022. The tiled cloakrooms were finished in May 2022.

The papers are House of Hackney’s own, hung through the rooms as specified for the showroom. This commission was internal works only.

The finished-room photographs marked “Photograph: House of Hackney” are House of Hackney’s own, from their website. The others were taken on site by us; the two marked “Before” show rooms as found, before the works began.

The last seven photographs are from an earlier job for the same client: House of Hackney’s previous showroom in Shoreditch, which we worked on in 2019. They are our own photographs, posted on our Instagram, [@mrwallcover](https://www.instagram.com/mrwallcover/), on 19 August 2019, and each is captioned as the earlier showroom. They are not St Michael’s Clergy House.

How the commission ran

## The same standards, on every commission.

Each commission has a written scope by room, walls prepared until they are true, protected floors, batch and shade control, set-out from the room’s focal points, and a return visit. [Read the method](https://www.mrwallcover.com/practice/#method).

The six standards in full

01

### Survey and scope, room by room

We measure the wall that will actually be hung, allow for the repeat and the wastage, and write a scope of works room by room before anyone orders paper.

02

### Preparation decides the finish

Walls are filled, made good and primed until they are true. If a wall is not ready for the material specified, we say so before the last drop is ordered.

03

### Protection and containment

Floors, furniture and finished joinery are protected as part of the hang. Work is contained and the place is left tidy each evening. In a home we are visitors; in a hotel we work around the house.

04

### Batch and shade control

Deliveries are checked against the measure, and batches and shading are managed so that a corridor of rooms reads as one surface.

05

### Set out from the room's focal points

Pattern is set out from chimneypieces, doorcases and bed walls, so the pattern sits square to the cornice and the joinery.

06

### One team, then the return visit

The people who start are the people who finish. Four to six weeks after completion we come back to look at every seam and edge, and the workmanship is guaranteed for twelve months.

[See the finish up close: seams, internal corners, edges and joins from our own installations](https://www.mrwallcover.com/details/)

By [Dorin Burcus](https://www.mrwallcover.com/about/#dorin), founder · Last updated 22 October 2026
